## Quick comparison

| | ENEMDU (Ecuador) | ENE (Chile) | ENOE (Mexico) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agency | INEC | INE | INEGI |
| Series origin | 1987 (predecessor), INEC since 1993 | 1966 | Jan 2005 (predecessors since 1972) |
| Frequency | Monthly, continuous | Monthly (*trimestre móvil*) | Continuous weekly collection; monthly + quarterly release |
| Last structural redesign | 2021–2024 (CEPAL-assisted), in force since Jan 2021 | 2020 (frame/calibration; kept inside the 2010 series) | COVID bridge 2020–2022, then a further re-launch Q1 2023 |
| Microdata comparable since* | Jan 2021 (current rotation scheme + UPM-level weighting) | Jan–Mar 2010 (*trimestre móvil* EFM 2010), with an identifier/weight seam at Oct–Dec 2019 | Q1 2023 (current classifiers + mixed-mode design); Q1 2014–Q1 2020 and 2005–2013 are separate, internally-consistent windows |
| COVID gap | Field suspended 16 Mar–Jun 2020; telephone bridge to Jul 2020 | No full suspension; shifted to phone/mixed from 2nd half of Mar 2020 | Field suspended Apr–Jun 2020; ETOE telephone survey, not part of the panel |
| Rotation scheme | 2(2)2 (monthly) | 3 submuestras × 6 rounds over 18 months | 5-quarter rotating panel |
| Overlap | 50% between quarters/years | 83.3% between consecutive waves of the same submuestra; 66.7% between consecutive published files | 80% quarter-to-quarter |
| Observation unit | Dwelling (*vivienda*) | Dwelling (*vivienda*) | Dwelling (*vivienda*); UPM fixed |

\* This is the window over which the sampling frame, rotation/identifier scheme, and weighting method are stable enough to build panels without extra harmonization work. It is **not** the same as an agency's own public "comparable" claim for headline indicators, which typically spans longer by absorbing methodology changes into the aggregates themselves (INEC states ENEMDU headline indicators are comparable back to June 2007; INEGI publishes ENOE 2005–present as one footnoted series). See §1.3, §2.3, §3.3 for the full reasoning behind each date.

## 1. ENEMDU (Ecuador, INEC)

### 1.1 How long has it been running?
The lineage goes back to the **Encuesta Permanente de Empleo y Desempleo**, run by INEM from **November 1987** with annual periodicity in urban areas. **INEC took over in 1993** "con la misma metodología, periodicidad y representatividad," and quarterly periodicity was established in September 2003 (*202605_Metodologia_ENEMDU*, p. 10). INEC's own user guide states the harmonized series is comparable back to **June 2007**:

> "La información estadística de la ENEMDU es comparable desde junio 2007."
> *Guía de Uso de Base de Datos ENEMDU 2021‑2024*, INEC

So: 39 years of lineage overall, 33 years under INEC, with an officially comparable window of ~19 years (2007–present) once the harmonized/homologated series is used.

### 1.2 Collection frequency
Monthly, continuous, all twelve months of the year: "La ENEMDU, es una encuesta de aplicación continua, la cual se realiza los doce meses del año" (*Diseño Muestral ENEMDU*, p. 5). Before 2021, only March/June/September/December had full public dissemination of labor-market results; the other eight months fed the Central Bank's Consumer Confidence Index and were not public. Since the 2021 redesign, monthly indicators (national + urban/rural) are published every month, with quarterly and annual aggregation adding city- and province-level representativity.

### 1.3 Last redesign: since when is data comparable?
The current design is the **ENEMDU 2021–2024/2026** redesign, done with CEPAL technical assistance and detailed in *"Recomendaciones Metodológicas para el Rediseño de la Encuesta Nacional Empleo, Desempleo y Subempleo (ENEMDU 2021–2024)"* (CEPAL, Jan 2021). It changed sample size/selection, the panel rotation scheme (2(2)2), and moved weighting to the UPM level. It took effect from **January 2021**.

Two things worth flagging for panel work:
- INEC's headline claim of comparability back to **June 2007** applies to the *harmonized indicator series*, not to the raw rotation/ID architecture: the sampling frame, rotation scheme, and weighting method are genuinely different pre- vs. post-2021, so 2021 is the right structural break for `panelaR`'s purposes even though INEC calls the headline numbers comparable further back.
- The panel rotation *design* itself has kept shifting inside the "2021–2026" era: the methodology document shows three distinct rotation graphics, one for 2021–2024, one for 2025 (Gráfico 2), and one for 2026 (Gráfico 3), with new panel-group codes appearing each time (e.g. `c32`→`c41`→`c51` as fresh UPM cohorts phase in).

### 1.4 COVID-19 impact
Yes, this is a genuine discontinuity, not just a mode change. Fieldwork was suspended on **March 16, 2020** (Decreto Ejecutivo 1017, CONEC Resolution 001‑2020), and the March 2020 round closed with only **48% coverage**, which INEC judged too spatially biased to publish. A stopgap operation, **ENEMDU Telefónica**, ran through roughly April–August 2020. Face-to-face fieldwork resumed in **July 2020** (initially mixed cara-a-cara + telephone). INEC explicitly could not produce an ENEMDU **annual 2020** release at all:

> "Para el 2020, no fue factible producir la ENEMDU anual, dado que, durante los meses
> de abril hasta agosto del 2020... la metodología de levantamiento fue telefónica y es
> incompatible con la agregación de muestra que requiere la ENEMDU anual."
> INEC, *ENEMDU Anual 2021* page

For practical purposes, the **March–August 2020** period should be treated as a structural gap for panel linkage: no reliable dwelling/person rotation continuity crosses this window, and INEC's own annual product simply skips 2020. The 2021–2024 redesign was explicitly framed as a pandemic-response measure ("dos lecciones que dejó la pandemia: estadísticas resilientes y oportunas," p. 11), which is why the redesign date and the COVID shock are tangled together in this survey specifically.

### 1.5 Current-series data issues (RECALCULADO and others)
Between September 2020 and May 2021, transitional methodological changes (sample size/distribution, representativity, weighting) broke comparability; INEC's fix was a retrospective recalculation:

> "...recalculando los indicadores desde septiembre 2020 hasta mayo 2021, con el fin de
> mantener la comparabilidad de las cifras."
> INEC, *ENEMDU Trimestral* page / *Nota técnica*, June 2021

Concretely, INEC republished the "Datos Abiertos" monthly files for that window with a `_RECALCULADO` suffix, alongside (in some cases) the original files. Other things worth keeping in mind:
- A separate, unrelated recalculation happened for the **2018 annual ENEMDU**, because that year's expansion factor had been built at the person level instead of the UPM level ("se realizó un recalculo de los estadísticos derivados").
- INEC changed the **folder-naming separator** (hyphen → underscore) on its file server in **mid‑2022**, a pure scraping/parsing quirk.

### 1.6 Rotation scheme
The scheme is **2(2)2**, in force since January 2021:

> "Cada grupo rotativo permanece dos períodos consecutivos, sale del estudio por otros
> dos periodos consecutivos, para volver a aparecer finalmente en los siguientes dos
> meses consecutivos."
> *Diseño Muestral ENEMDU*, p. 21

In practice: a dwelling group is interviewed in two consecutive months, sits out the next two months (its slot is filled by a different rotation group), then reappears for two more months. Both the UPM and the dwellings-within-UPM rotate; panel codes are a letter + 2 digits, where the first two characters identify the UPM's rotation group and the third digit identifies which of the two dwelling sub-groups within that UPM is being surveyed. This yields a **50% overlap** between consecutive quarters and years:

> "...se establece un traslape del 50% de la muestra entre trimestres y años..."
> *Diseño Muestral ENEMDU*, p. 21

### 1.7 Observation unit for rotation
The **dwelling** (*vivienda*) is the unit of observation for the panel/rotation design:

> "...el seguimiento se realiza a nivel de viviendas (unidad de observación)."
> *Diseño Muestral ENEMDU*, p. 21

UPMs also rotate in a slower cycle (new UPM cohorts phase in over time), but the tracked/followed unit within a UPM is the dwelling: `id_persona` is a roster slot, not a stable person key, so `id_vivienda` is the legitimate longitudinal anchor.

## 2. ENE (Chile, INE)

### 2.1 How long has it been running?
ENE is one of the oldest continuous household surveys in Latin America, with origins in **1966**:

> "...la ENE tiene origen en el año 1966... siendo una de las encuestas continuas más
> antiguas de América Latina (Cecchini, 2005)."
> *Documento Metodológico ENE*, p. 10

INE identifies three periods: **1966–1985** (installation; known as ECMO, *Encuesta Continua de Mano de Obra*, until 1972, took the name "Encuesta Nacional de Empleo" for the first time in 1975), **1986–2009** (national consolidation, monthly publication via *trimestre móvil* introduced), and **2010–present** (major conceptual/methodological modernization aligned with the ILO's 19th ICLS). That's roughly **60 years** of series history overall.

### 2.2 Collection frequency
Monthly, via **rolling quarters** (*trimestre móvil*): interviews happen continuously across three rotating submuestras, and each month's release reports on the trailing three-month window. E.g., the July release covers April–June. Consecutive monthly releases therefore share two of their three reference months.

### 2.3 Last redesign: since when is data comparable?
The **currently valid ("vigente") series starts at the rolling quarter January–March (EFM) 2010**:

> "...los datos de la serie vigente no son comparables con series anteriores de la ENE,
> debido a la incorporación de importantes cambios conceptuales y metodológicos a partir
> de enero-marzo de 2010."
> *Libro de Códigos ENE*, p. 13

A further update took effect in **2020**: new sampling frame (**MMV 2017**, built from the 2017 Census), new questionnaire dimensions, and a new calibration method (raking to 2017 Census population projections). Importantly, **INE did not treat 2020 as starting a new series**: the calibrated weight (`fact_cal`) is explicitly valid for the whole 2010–present run: "Vigente para la totalidad de la serie, desde EFM 2010" (*Libro de Códigos ENE*, p. 68). So for `panelaR` purposes, **2010 is the real comparability boundary**, not 2020; the 2020 change is a within-series frame/weighting refresh.

One caveat that matters for weighting: bases published before the Oct–Dec 2019 quarter carry **two incompatible expansion factors**: `fact` (traditional, Census 2002-based, discontinued after OND 2019) and `fact_cal` (Census 2017-based, raking). Only `fact_cal` spans the full series, so always use it, never `fact`, when pooling pre-/post-2020 data.

INE also runs an **annual revision policy**, official since February 2020, under which figures can be retrospectively revised every **July**:

> "El proceso de revisión se lleva a cabo en julio de cada año."
> *Libro de Códigos ENE*, p. 14

This is why download-date versioning matters: the current *Libro de Códigos* file explicitly notes it reflects the **July 2025** revision.

### 2.4 COVID-19 impact
The 2020 frame/methodology transition was already underway before COVID hit, and the pandemic forced an *additional* change mid-transition: field collection shifted from face-to-face to phone/mixed from the second half of March 2020 onward. The old paper-based system (COENE, used for the legacy MMS/MMM frame, "muestra antigua") was only fully retired in **June 2020**, once the frame transition to MMV 2017 completed and all units moved to the mobile-device system (SIENE/DMC).

Two consequences worth tracking:
- Some published series were **discontinued and later resumed**: certain provincial/conurbación breakdowns stop at the January–March 2020 quarter and only resume at June–August 2021 (*Documento Metodológico ENE*, Table 23 footnote).
- The rotation design itself was disrupted: normally 1/6 of dwellings refresh every quarter, but pandemic-era contact problems meant some dwellings **could not be substituted on schedule and stayed in the panel past their sixth round**:

  > "...cierta proporción de la muestra no pudo ser sustituida y por ende permaneció por
  > más de seis rondas en la muestra."
  > *Documento Metodológico ENE*, p. 91

For practical purposes, the period of March 2020–2021 should be treated as a period where the assumption of "exactly 6 rounds, then rotate out" does not hold. If you're deriving a round/tenure variable for panel matching, this window needs a data-driven check rather than an assumption based on the nominal design.

### 2.5 Current-series data issues
- **Two incompatible expansion factors** before/after OND 2019 (§2.3): always use `fact_cal`.
- **Annual July revision policy** can retroactively rewrite parts of the series: version by download date, exactly as you're already doing.
- **`id_identificacion` conflates dwelling and household**: no separate dwelling identifier. However, codebook also documents an explicit person-level longitudinal key, `idrph`, described as "Identificador único de personas. Esta variable permite identificar a las personas encuestadas de forma longitudinal" (*Libro de Códigos ENE*, p. 124), which may be a more direct starting point than reconstructing person links from `id_identificacion` + roster line, though its stability still needs some kind of empirical check.
- **Deduplication of stacked rolling-quarter files**: confirmed still the right approach, filter `mes_central == mes_encuesta`.
- **Pandemic-era rotation stretch** (§2.4): open item for validating panel depth in 2020–2021.

### 2.6 Rotation scheme
The total sample is split into **three submuestras**, interviewed on a fixed monthly cycle:

> "...durante los meses de enero, abril, julio y octubre de cada año, son entrevistadas
> las viviendas de la submuestra 1... febrero, mayo, agosto y noviembre las viviendas de
> la submuestra 2... marzo, junio, septiembre y diciembre [la submuestra 3]."
> *Documento Metodológico ENE*, p. 65

Each dwelling is interviewed for **6 rounds**, one every three months, over **18 months** total, after which it's replaced:

> "Las viviendas seleccionadas se entrevistan en seis ocasiones o rondas... a lo largo de
> 18 meses, con intervalos de tres meses entre cada entrevista."
> *Documento Metodológico ENE*, p. 90

Each rolling quarter, **1/18 of the total ENE sample** is refreshed (one submuestra's one-sixth cohort). This gives two distinct overlap figures that are easy to conflate, worth keeping straight:
- **83.3% (5/6)** overlap between consecutive appearances of the *same* submuestra (i.e., household-level rotation overlap, quarter to quarter for that submuestra).
- **66.7% (2/3)** overlap between consecutive *published* rolling-quarter files, since each release shares two of its three reference months with the prior release.

### 2.7 Observation unit for rotation
The dwelling is the sampling/rotation unit; information is then collected for all usual residents within it:

> "...la unidad de selección en la muestra es la vivienda, la recolección de la
> información se realiza a nivel de las personas..."
> *Documento Metodológico ENE*, p. 94

## 3. ENOE (Mexico, INEGI)

### 3.1 How long has it been running?
ENOE itself started in **January 2005**, replacing two predecessor surveys: ENEU (urban, 1985–2004) and ENE (rural supplement, bianual 1991–1995, annual 1996–2000, quarterly Q2 2000–Q4 2004):

> "Su puesta en marcha en enero de 2005 marcó el fin del modelo de captación y
> procesamiento de la Encuesta Nacional de Empleo Urbano (ENEU) y de la Encuesta
> Nacional de Empleo (ENE)."
> *Cómo se hace la ENOE*, Presentación

The lineage goes back further still: ENH (1972–73) → ECMO (1973–74) → ECSO (1974–84) → ENEU (1985–2004) + ENE (1988/1991–2004) → ENOE (2005–present). So: **~21 years** as ENOE specifically, **~54 years** of household labor-force survey tradition in Mexico.

### 3.2 Collection frequency
Continuous **weekly** field collection ("semanalmente de lunes a domingo, durante todo el año"), released **monthly** (headline indicators) and **quarterly** (full microdata, with state and city representativity).

### 3.3 Last redesign: since when is data comparable?
This is genuinely more layered than a single redesign date, and it's important not to collapse it into just "the COVID break." There are **three distinct vintages**:

1. **Original ENOE, Q1 2005–Q1 2020**: face-to-face, the design documented in *Cómo se hace la ENOE* (2020 ed.).
2. **ENOE Nueva Edición (ENOEN), Q3 2020–Q4 2022**: a COVID-era bridge series, mixed face-to-face/telephone (~72%/28% initially).
3. **Current ENOE, Q1 2023–present**: INEGI describes this as resuming "regular" ENOE operation, but under an updated methodology:

   > "A partir del primer trimestre de 2023, se retomó la operación regular de la ENOE...
   > Este programa estadístico incluye dentro de su metodología la captación de
   > información a través de entrevistas cara a cara y telefónicas; la actualización a
   > los clasificadores vigentes para los campos de parentesco, planes de estudio,
   > países, ocupación y actividad económica; y la incorporación de las preguntas de
   > migración y lugar de trabajo."
   > INEGI, ENOE 2025 metadata catalog (RNM)

INEGI's published tables present 2005–present as one continuous headline series (with footnotes on which population-estimate vintage applies to which quarters), but for microdata/panel work each of the three vintages has a genuinely different sampling frame, collection-mode mix, and, as of 2023, different classifiers. Treat **Q1 2023** as a second, separate structural break from the COVID one, not a mere continuation of ENOEN.

Separately, and unrelated to COVID: the sampling frame moved from **MMV 2002** (built from the 2000 Census) to **MMV 2012** (built from the 2010 Census) via a staggered, panel-by-panel substitution that started in 2013 and completed in **Q4 2013**, so **Q1 2014** is the first quarter fully on the newer frame, and 2013 quarters mix both frames across different rotation panels. Geographic coverage also expanded (more autorrepresentada cities) starting **Q3 2017**.

### 3.4 COVID-19 impact
Field collection was suspended entirely for **April–June 2020** and reactivated on **July 17, 2020**. In its place, INEGI ran the **ETOE** (*Encuesta Telefónica de Ocupación y Empleo*), a standalone monthly telephone survey for April, May, and June 2020, explicitly *not* a methodological continuation of ENOE:

> "Se precisa que el dato de la ETOE no puede ser metodológicamente una continuidad de la
> serie de la ENOE; se incluye sólo con fines [de referencia]."
> INEGI, *Comunicado de Prensa 264/20*

Two nuances worth knowing:
- ETOE re-contacted a subset of the same people interviewed in ENOE Q1 2020, so a **one-off panel link** between ENOE-2020Q1 and ETOE-Apr/May/Jun exists and has been used in academic work (e.g., tracking ~18,000 individuals' transitions through the lockdown). This is *not* part of INEGI's regular rotation/panel microdata, though, so don't expect it to slot into the standard 5-quarter panel machinery.
- In INEGI's own official aggregate historical tables, the **Q2 2020** cell is filled using "el promedio de los resultados mensuales de la [ETOE]", an aggregate-indicator splice, not a microdata-level fix.

For practical purposes, **Q2 2020 should be treated as a full missing quarter** in the regular ENOE rotating panel: no microdata, no rotation continuity across it. ENOEN restarts in Q3 2020; before assuming any `t−1` link across the Q1→Q3 2020 gap, verify empirically whether ENOEN's Q3 2020 panels were freshly drawn or partially carried over from the interrupted Q1 2020 panels (INEGI's public documentation doesn't state this explicitly either way in what's on file here, so this is a genuine open question, not something resolved in the methodology PDF).

### 3.5 Current-series data issues
- **Three vintages, two breaks**: Q1 2020/Q3 2020 (COVID) and Q4 2022/Q1 2023 (classifier and mode-standardization change), both need to be treated as structural boundaries for panel work, not just the COVID one.
- **Multiple population-weight revisions**, applied retroactively to different windows: CONAPO 2013 projections were the base for years, but starting **Q1 2021** INEGI began phasing in continuous population estimates from its own Marco de Muestreo de Viviendas, applied gradually backward across quarters; published tables footnote which quarters use which population base. Same principle as Chile: **version by download date**.
- **2013 frame transition** (MMV 2002 → MMV 2012) is staggered *within* rotation panels, not a clean quarter cutoff; worth a specific check if you build ENOE panels spanning 2013.
- **2017 coverage expansion** (more autorrepresentada cities from Q3 2017) affects which cities have city-representative panels before vs. after that date.

### 3.6 Rotation scheme
Five rotation panels, with an **80% quarter-to-quarter overlap**:

> "La muestra tiene un traslape del 80% de un trimestre a otro... La muestra se dividió
> en cinco submuestras llamados paneles de rotación."
> *Cómo se hace la ENOE*, p. 52

Each dwelling is visited **once per quarter for five consecutive quarters**, then replaced: 1/5 (20%) of the sample rotates out (and a fresh 1/5 rotates in) every quarter:

> "A cada vivienda seleccionada se le visita una vez por trimestre en el trascurso de
> cinco trimestres."
> *Cómo se hace la ENOE*, p. 52

This is the classic "0/I/II/III/IV" rotating-panel design (conceptually similar in spirit to the US CPS's rotation logic, though ENOE's is a plain 5-wave-then-out design without CPS's 8-month gap).

### 3.7 Observation unit for rotation
UPMs are fixed over time; the **dwelling** is what actually rotates:

> "...la muestra seleccionada de UPM permanece fija en el tiempo y solo se renuevan las
> viviendas habitadas en cada uno de los trimestres..."
> *Cómo se hace la ENOE*, p. 78

Dwelling is the tracked unit, persons are enumerated within it at each visit, with only the first visit ("apertura") capturing full sociodemographic detail and later visits updating select items.

## 4. Cross-survey notes for panel construction

- **All three surveys anchor the panel at the dwelling**, not the household or the person, consistent with the architectural choice you already made in `panelaR` (match persons within dwellings, derive household crosswalks afterward). Nothing here suggests a survey-specific exception to that pattern, though ENE Chile's conflated `id_identificacion` (dwelling+household together) means the *dwelling→household* step needs its own logic for Chile, distinct from ENEMDU's `id_vivienda`.
- **Every survey has at least one COVID-era gap that breaks rotation continuity**: Ecuador (Mar–Aug 2020, telephone bridge, no annual 2020 release), Mexico (Apr–Jun 2020 fully missing, ETOE non-comparable), Chile (no full suspension, but rotation depth itself was disrupted through 2020–2021). None of the three can be treated as a clean, uninterrupted panel across 2020.
- **Every survey has an official retrospective-revision mechanism** that changes published figures after the fact: Ecuador's RECALCULADO (Sep 2020–May 2021, one-time), Chile's annual July revision policy (recurring, every year), Mexico's rolling population-estimate updates (recurring, ad hoc). This argues for the same discipline across all three pipelines: **always record the download date and treat historical windows as potentially versioned**, not just for Ecuador.
- **Ecuador is the only one of the three with an official matched-quarter product** (INEC's Matriz de Transición Laboral / Base Match) that you can use as an external validation benchmark, as you're already doing via `enemdu_download_match()`. Chile and Mexico don't appear (in the documents on file) to publish an equivalent official matched panel product: INE and INEGI release rotation-group codes and let users build their own links, which is closer to what `panelaR` needs to do from scratch for those two countries.
- **Rotation-scheme "shape" differs enough that no matching logic should transfer directly**: ENEMDU is monthly with a 2-on/2-off/2-on structure (lags of 3 and 9 months); ENE is monthly-published but quarter-spaced per dwelling (lags of 3 months per round, 6 rounds over 18 months, with two *different* overlap statistics depending on whether you're comparing submuestra-to-submuestra or file-to-file); ENOE is cleanly quarterly with a flat 5-wave design (lag of 1 quarter, up to 4 lags before a dwelling exits). The `{3, 9}` lag pair that works for ENEMDU has no ENE or ENOE equivalent: ENE's natural lags are {3} within a submuestra's rounds, and ENOE's natural lag is simply {1 quarter}, repeatable up to 4 times per dwelling.
